records.full_text:
Norway
Regulation No. 1385 on regulating fishing in 2012 by Swedish vessels in the economic zone south of 62° N.
The Regulation applies to the fishing in the economic zone by Swedish vessels. These are only authorized to quantities of catch in the Norwegian economic zone south of 62° N, between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the coast, and west from a straight line through Lindesnes and Hanstholmen lighthouses. The Swedish flagged vessels may fish a total allowable catch of cod (382 tons), haddock (707 tons), pollock (880), Pollachius Pollachius/Merlangius Merlangus (190 tons), mackerel and bycatch thereof (242 tons), forage fish (800 tons), of which maximum 400 tons of horse mackerel, herring (922), shrimps (123 tons) and other species in the same quantities. Bycatch of cod, haddock, saithe, pollack and Merlangius Merlangus shall be calculated against quotas for these species. Catches of mackerel when fishing for herring is limited to maximum bycatch of 10% weight of each catch.
Original title
FOR 2011-12-14 nr 1385: Forskrift om regulering av fisket med fartøy som fører svensk flagg i Norges økonomiske sone sør for 62° N i 2012.
Entry into force notes

records.full_text:
Norway (Jan Mayen)
Regulation No. 1912 regulating fishing by Faroense vessels in Norwegian economic zone and fishing area in Jan Mayen in 2015.
It is prohibited to engage in fishing and trapping for vessels flying Faroese flag in the Norwegian Economic Zone and the areas around Jan Mayen between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the baselines. Notwithstanding the prohibition, Faroese vessels have access to the Norwegian economic zone north of 62° N between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the baselines and is permitted the following limited fishing quota: 4 121 tons of cod, 900 tons of haddock, 800 tons of saithe, 200 tons of other species as bycatch, including redfish and Greenland halibut. Vessels flying the Faroese flag have also access to fish 46 485 tons of the Faroe Islands national quota of mackerel in the Economic Zone and the fishery zone around Jan Mayen; additionally, they are allowed to fish the following quantities assigned to the Faroe Islands by Russia in the Norwegian economic zone north of 62 ° between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the baselines: a) 10 000 tons of cod, b) 900 tons of haddock, and c) 200 tons of other species, including redfish and Greenland halibut bycatch. When fishing for other species, it is permitted to have up to 20% of weight of redfish in each catch and in landed catch.

Forskrift om regulering av fisket for fartøy som fører færøysk flagg i Norges økonomiske sone og i fiskerisonen ved Jan Mayen i 2015.

records.full_text:
Norway
Decree No. 1001 of 1993 relative to the carrying out of control of foreign vessels involved in fishing or hunting activities in the Norwegian economic zone north of 62° N.- Repealed
This Directive of the Director of Fisheries concerns the reporting for control of foreign fishing vessels in the Norwegian Economic Zone to the coast guard. Section 1 gives the control stations where vessels shall report after termination of fishing activities. Vessels which plan to land fish in the zone in a Norwegian port shall report this to the nearest control station. Notification shall take place at least 24 hours before arrival at the control station. The notification may be send together with the passive reporting in accordance with section 8 of the Decree relative to foreign fishing in the Norwegian Economic Zone of 13 May 1977. (3 sections)

records.full_text:
Norway
Decree relative to installation of gear for other fish than anadromous salmon (No. 289 of 1989).
This Decree of the Ministry of Environment regulates the lowering into the water of gear. Gear with a mesh size of 35 mm and larger used for marine fisheries shall in the period of 1 May until 30 September be installed in such way that the main parts are at least 3 meters under the level of the water in any tide. This requirement can be extended to gear of any mesh size by the County Chief. The requirement shall not apply to commercial fishing for other fish than anadromous salmon by fishermen included in the Fishermen's Census and set out from vessels registered in the Marks Register. (5 sections)

records.full_text:
Norway
Regulation No. 1901 regulating fishing by Greenlandic vessels in Norwegian economic zone south of 62° N in 2015.
It is prohibited to engage in fishing and trapping for vessels flying Greenlandic flag in the Economic Zone between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the baselines. Notwithstanding the prohibition, Greenlandic vessels have access to the Norwegian economic zone north of 62° N between 12 and 200 nautical miles from the baselines and is permitted the following limited fishing quota: 3 500 tons of cod, 900 tons of haddock, 700 tons of saithe, 260 tons of other species as bycatch, including redfish and Greenland halibut. Following an application from Greenland to Norwegian fishery authorities with the assumption of Russian acceptance, the Greenlandic vessels are permitted to fish in the Norwegian economic zone north of 62° N part of the quotas of cod and haddock awarded by Russia. Greenlandic vesses may have access to fish 5 100 tons of cod and 500 tons of haddock, quantities allocated to Greenland from Russia in the Norwegian economic zone north of 62° N.
When fishing for other species, it is permitted to have up to 20% mixture of redfish in each catch and in landed catch.

Norway
Decree No. 1566 of 2010 to regulate fishing by vessels of Sweden in the Norwegian Economic Zone south of 62° in 2011.
This Decree prohibits in principle fishing by vessels of Sweden in the Norwegian EEZ but grants Sweden for 2011 the right to fish a specified total allowable catch south of 62nd parallel in a zone between the 12 and 200 nautical miles calculated from the baseline of Norway and west of a straight line between Lindesnes and Hansholmen of: cod, haddock, mackerel including bycatch, coalfish, whiting/pollack, industry fish including a bycatch of horse mackerel, herring, shrimps and other kind of fishes on a traditional scale. Bycatch of mentioned fish species shall be included in the quota. Bycatch of mackerel in herring fishing shall be limited to 10 percent. records.full_text:
Norway
Decree No. 1401 of 2008 to regulate fishing by vessels of Sweden in the Norwegian Economic Zone south of 62° in 2009.
This Decree grants Sweden for 2009 the right to fish a specified total allowable catch south of 62nd parallel in a zone between the 12 and 200 nautical miles calculated from the baseline of Norway and west of a straight line between Lindesnes and Hansholmen of: cod, haddock, mackerel including bycatch, coalfish, whiting/pollack, industry fish including a bycatch of horse mackerel, herring, shrimps and other kind of fishes on a traditional scale. Bycatch of mentioned fish species shall be included in the quota. Bycatch of mackerel in herring fishing shall be limited to 10 percent. It is forbidden to catch mackerel smaller than 30 cm and herring smaller than 20 cm. Fifteen percent of undersized fish is allowed in the catch of mackerel and 10 percent of undersized fish in the catch of herring. The Director of Fisheries may issue directions regarding reporting. Offences shall be punished pursuant to sections 8 and 9 of Act No. 91 of 1976.
Original title
